intro: The product configurator pack, for made-to-order products: set out the options a customer chooses from and the rules between them, then price a configuration and put it on a quotation, with its cost, margin, parts and lead time worked out as you go. Switch the pack on in Organisation › Settings › Industry packs.
start: Turn the product configurator pack on in Organisation › Settings › Industry packs.
Make a product configurable on Configurable products, with its base price, cost and lead time.
Add its options, values and rules, and check them with Try it.
Publish the product, then configure it for a customer and put it on a quotation.

articles.title: Make a product configurable
articles.summary: Choose the product it sells as, set its base price, cost and lead time, add the options a customer picks from, then publish it.

steps.lead: Choose the product it sells as,
steps.rest: then give it a name, a base price, a base cost and the lead time before options. Choose the bill of materials it starts from, if it has one.
for each thing the customer chooses. Give it a label and say whether it is asked as a choice, a number or yes or no.
for each answer, with its price change (a fixed amount or a percent of the base), any lead days it adds and any parts it adds to the bill of materials.
from the actions when it is ready. It can now be configured for customers.

tips: Tick The customer must choose on an option that needs an answer. Publishing needs a value for every such option.
Retiring a product keeps the configurations already saved.

articles.title: Add rules so only sensible choices can be made
articles.summary: Rules stop combinations that cannot be built, limit one option by another, and add parts or time when a choice needs them.

steps.rest: from Options and rules, and press Add a rule.
Not allowed, Needs, Adds a part or Takes longer.

steps.lead: Under When, say what sets it off,
steps.rest: such as one option being set a certain way, or a number from one amount to another.
the values the option cannot be or can only be, the part it adds and its price, or the working days added.
It shows as a plain sentence under Rules. Switch it off or on later without deleting it.
Choose any options and see the price, cost and lead time worked out. Nothing is saved.

tips: If a rule rules out a default value, the first allowed value is used instead and you are told why.

articles.title: Configure a product for a customer and quote it
articles.summary: Choose the options and see the price, margin, parts, stock and lead time at once, then save it and put it on a quotation.

steps.rest: and choose the product and the customer.
and set how many. Anything not allowed says why.
the price, the cost, margin and time, and the bill of materials with what is in stock and what is short.
if they need to know something.

steps.lead: Press Save and put on a quotation.
steps.rest: The quotation is made with one line for the configuration at its configured price. Or press Save the configuration to keep it as a draft.

tips: A configuration cannot be saved while something blocks it, such as a required option left empty. The page says what it is.
A margin under your minimum is flagged, and your settings can refuse the quote.
Price books, discounts and approval limits apply on the quotation, after the configured price.
On Configurations, a draft can be changed or cancelled from Actions, and a quoted one links to its quotation.
